newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: No injury in Prague Metro smoke incident - operator.
newsitem.headline: No injury in Prague Metro smoke incident - operator.

text.p: Smoke poured into a tunnel in a central section of Prague's Metro underground railway on Monday, but no one was injured, a spokeswoman for the system's operator, DP Metro, told Reuters.
Zuzana Knoblochova said smoke in the tunnel between two stations forced a partial suspension of services on the system's A line, but the reasons for the incident were not yet known.

"At 9:45 (0745 GMT) operation on line A was limited. There was smoke in the tunnel between station Square of Peace (Namesti Miru) and station George of Podebrady (Jiriho z Podebrad)," Knoblochova said.
"The fire crew is on the spot now. The reasons are being investigated."

Earlier the CTK agency had quoted an emergency official as saying about 30 people had been examined on the spot or taken to hospital. Knoblochova said she could not confirm the number of people who were examined, but she said there were no injuries.
CTK quoted a fireman as saying the incident might have been due to an electrical short circuit causing a fire in the tunnel.
Line A is the second oldest of the three lines on the Prague system, which has been functioning since the late 1970s.
